layers.note: One of the leading tall herbs of Cascade subalpine meadows, in broad patches, and in the herb layer of open subalpine forest.

moisture.note: Moist meadow and forest ground; not in standing water.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; thickest on cool, snowy slopes.

elevation_m.note: Near sea level in the north to about 2,500 m; mostly montane to subalpine in Washington.

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to part shade under open conifers.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −16 to 2 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 6 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −38 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 17 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 21 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 3,200 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 1,700 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.5, gone by 0.35.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.55 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.75.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Sitka valerian grows from Alaska and Yukon to northern California, Idaho and Montana, in moist montane and subalpine meadows and woods (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
